name: Firmware for a custom board
description: For firmware on a microcontroller board, for example STM32. Put the PCB layout, schematic and CubeMX .ioc file in the project folder, or just name the board in the requirement. A board researcher works out the hardware, a rig engineer sets up how the AI flashes and tests the real board, and the tests run on the hardware itself.

steps.name: Board researcher
steps.purpose: Works out what is on the board and how it is wired, from the files you gave or from the internet when you only named the board.
reads: the .ioc, schematic, PCB layout and BOM files in this workspace
the board and MCU documentation online
produces: .devcrew/hardware/board.md: MCU, clocks, pin table, external parts, programming and serial interfaces, sources, assumptions and conflicts

steps.name: HIL rig engineer
steps.purpose: Sets up how the AI can flash the real board, watch its serial output and run tests on it, without two runs using the same board at once.
reads: the build files in this workspace (Makefile, CMakeLists.txt, .ioc)
produces: .devcrew/hil/: rig.json, probe.sh, flash.sh, monitor.sh, run.sh with a per-board lock, and RIG.md with setup steps and the commands tests call

steps.title: Review the board, the test rig and the plan

steps.name: Firmware reviewer
steps.purpose: Checks the firmware against the real board and sends it back to Dev if it would misbehave on the hardware.
produces: .devcrew/firmware-review.md: a verdict and hardware-related findings by severity
